## Audit Report: Mirror-Mad Phantasm

**Status: ISSUE**

Two bugs found, both in edge cases:

### Issue 1 — Library exhaustion incorrectly kills the player (engine bug)

The reveal loop calls `draw_top_card()` to pull cards off the top of the library. When the library is exhausted without finding "Mirror-Mad Phantasm" (e.g., Necrotic Ooze has the ability and no actual Mirror-Mad Phantasm card is in the library), `draw_top_card()` at `state.rs:1315` sets `has_drawn_from_empty = true`. After `on_activate_ability` returns, SBAs see this flag and mark the player as having lost.

Per the ruling: *"If no card named Mirror-Mad Phantasm is revealed ... all cards from that library will be put into their owner's graveyard."* — the game continues. It is not a "draw from an empty library" loss condition; revealing is not drawing.

In normal play (Mirror-Mad Phantasm the card activates its own ability) this bug is dormant, because the card is always in the library and is always found. It manifests when no actual Mirror-Mad Phantasm exists in the library.

### Issue 2 — Token copy is incorrectly "found" and put onto the battlefield (engine bug)

A token copy of Mirror-Mad Phantasm (e.g., via Cackling Counterpart) shares Mirror-Mad Phantasm's `card_id` and therefore has the activated ability. When it activates, `move_object(token, Zone::Library)` runs but SBAs (rule 704.5d: tokens cease to exist when not on the battlefield) have not run yet. The reveal loop finds the token by name (`"Mirror-Mad Phantasm"`) before the library is exhausted and puts it on the battlefield. After the ability resolves, SBAs don't remove it because it is back on the battlefield.

Per the ruling: *"If no card named Mirror-Mad Phantasm is revealed (possibly because ... it was a token), all cards from that library will be put into their owner's graveyard."* — the token should be treated as no longer existing; all library cards should be milled.

### Test coverage
There is one test (`tier15_cards.rs:2553`) covering the normal "finds itself" case, but it calls `on_activate_ability` directly (bypassing the engine's SBA loop, mana payment, and trigger processing). No tests cover the library-exhaustion case, the token-copy case, the Necrotic Ooze scenario, or the opponent-controls-MMP ownership split.
